title: STDec: Spatio-Temporal Stability Guided Decoding for dLLMs
claim: Our method gives a better speed-quality trade-off than existing acceleration baselines across many benchmarks and models.
layout: 2 panels, radar chart left, scatter plot right, shared legend below
description: A two-panel results figure with a shared legend strip along the bottom. The left panel is a radar chart over eight benchmarks. Math, MBPP, HumanEval, GPQA and GSM8K sit on a blue arc labelled Textual Reasoning. MathVista, MathVision and MathVerse sit on a green arc labelled Multimodal Understanding. Ten methods are drawn as colored polygons, and the green STDec polygon encloses all the others. The right panel is a scatter plot of averaged benchmark score against throughput in tokens per second. It is split into three horizontal bands for Dream, LLaDA and LaViDa. In each band, a grey vanilla baseline has a dashed red arrow to a green STDec point, labelled with speedups of 10.03×, 7.60× and 3.57×. The title 'Efficiency-Quality Trade-off' with a smiley sits in the center. The legend maps colors and shapes to the ten methods.
caption: Efficiency-quality trade-off compared with existing acceleration approaches. Across eight benchmarks (left) and three models (right), \modelname{} achieves a strong trade-off between throughput and quality, consistently delivering higher generation efficiency while preserving competitive overall performance on both textual reasoning and multimodal understanding tasks.
abstract: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) have achieved rapid progress, viewed as a promising alternative to the autoregressive paradigm. However, most dLLM decoders still adopt a global confidence threshold, and do not explicitly model local context from neighboring decoded states or temporal consistency of predicted token IDs across steps. To address this issue, we propose a spatio-temporal stability guided decoding approach, named STDec. We observe strong spatio-temporal stability in dLLM decoding: newly decoded tokens tend to lie near decoded neighbors, and their predicted IDs often remain consistent across several denoising steps. Inspired by this stability, our STDec introduces spatial-aware decoding and temporal-aware decoding. The spatial-aware decoding dynamically generates the token-adaptive thresholds by aggregating the decoded states of nearby tokens. The temporal-aware decoding relaxes the decoding thresholds for tokens whose predicted token IDs remain consistent over denoising steps. Our STDec is training-free and remains compatible with cache-based acceleration methods. Across textual reasoning and multimodal understanding benchmarks, STDec achieves improved inference throughput while maintaining comparable generation score. Notably, on MBPP with LLaDA, STDec achieves up to 14.17$\times$ speedup with a comparable score. The homepage is available at https://yzchen02.github.io/STDec.
